column1: # Batch 31 — the --check-filter run CLAUDE.md asked for, 2026-10-06.
# CLAUDE.md said of these tables: "333 of them are entity pivots that have not
# been run against a real entity, nor --check-filter'ed (rules 4 and 4d) ...
# Treat those pivots as registered, not proven, until they are verified." This
# is that run, against all 360 rows of docs/candidate-sources-batch31.*.txt,
# every one of which was registered in the binary at the time.
# 51 PASS. The rest did not, and one verdict is not a quality score but a
# defect: 65 rows came back FILTER_IGNORED — the upstream accepts the entity
# parameter, ignores it, and returns the same collection for a real entity and
# for one that cannot exist. Rule 4d calls that "worse than a source that
# returns nothing: it is a confident wrong answer", and CLAUDE.md says to treat
# it as fatal. Those 65 were removed from the hp3b31_*.c tables; the registry
# went 18,643 -> 18,578 and both floors were re-recorded.
# Two were confirmed by hand before any row was touched, because 65 live
# sources is not something to delete on one tool's say-so:
# The remaining non-PASS rows are NOT removed here. A single probe is one
# reading, and HTTP_ERR/NET_ERR/TIMEOUT can be transient, a user-agent, or a
# host having a bad afternoon — whereas FILTER_IGNORED is a property of the
# endpoint's query handling and does not come and go. They now disclose
# themselves instead: lib/hpengine.c stores a collector-fetch-failure record
# naming the status, so a refused fetch is no longer indistinguishable from a
# source that ran and found nothing.
# Verdict counts: HTTP_ERR=146, FILTER_IGNORED=65, PASS=51, UNPARSEABLE=39, NET_ERR=31, FILTER_UNCHECKED=11, EMPTY_RESULTSET=6, TIMEOUT=5, PATH_UNRESOLVED=2, ERR=2, PATH_NOT_ARRAY=1, EMPTY=1
